signals_considered.why_nothing_published:
Of the 36 groups clearing the up-threshold, the top of the table is almost entirely WPI-driven: crude +10.70 (WPI Crude Petroleum 3m +85.6%), silver +10.16 (WPI Silver 12m +152.4%), sulphuric acid +6.97 (WPI Sulphuric Acid 1m +20.9%), carbon black +4.43, zinc +4.39, caustic soda +3.20, tea +3.10. Every one of those 1m/3m/12m changes ENDS IN APRIL 2026. A seven-month-old wholesale index is not a price that moved today, and publishing a company on it would be publishing on a stale number. Today's actual dated prints point the other way: Brent -20.2% on the month, copper -18.3%, naphtha -22.2%.

The one strong group resting on something other than WPI is **dye intermediates (+4.29)**, driven by DGCI&S customs data for September 2026 - H-acid export unit price +42.9% on the month, +25.0% on three months, +49.2% on the same month a year earlier. Two mapped small caps there are unpublished: AksharChem (Rs 271 cr; the map records H-acid capacity 1,200 t with FY26 output 785 t and vinyl sulphone 7,800 t from AR 2025-26) and Shree Pushkar Chemicals (Rs 1,667 cr). Neither was researched today: the government lane took the research budget, and two-month-old customs data is a weaker trigger than a Cabinet decision taken this afternoon. **Recorded as the first commodity candidate for the next run.**
signals_considered.mapping_problem_found: The **paper and pulp** group (+3.08) is headlined by HS 4707 waste-paper IMPORT unit price +46.2% over three months and lists Andhra Paper and Seshasayee Paper as `benefit`. Waste paper is an INPUT to a recycled-paper mill, so a rising import price is a cost, not a gain. The direction of that mapping looks wrong and is logged for the owner - commodity_map.json was NOT edited, because the exposure was not read from either company's filings in this run.

researched.name: Indo Farm Equipment Ltd
researched.reason: Rs 547.8 cr maker of 9-30 t hydraulic pick & carry cranes and 16-110 HP tractors at Baddi. Cranes were Rs 21,809.19 lakh of Rs 44,002.05 lakh of FY26 consolidated revenue (49.6%) per its own Integrated Annual Report, so roughly half the company is construction equipment - the subject of today's Rs 11,000 cr Cabinet scheme. The publishable fact is not the scheme, though: the FY26 annual report says the existing crane plant ran at ~80% utilisation and that 'capacity, not demand, has been the binding constraint', and Infomerics' 18-Sep-2026 rating UPGRADE (IVR A/Stable, IVR A1) documents a new Bhud plant adding 3,600 cranes a year for Rs 71.13 cr of project cost, operational in H2 FY27. At the Rs 21.3 lakh per crane derived from the segment accounts, management's own FY28 ramp of 1,500-1,800 units is Rs 320-384 cr of incremental revenue against a company that did Rs 440 cr in FY26 - from Rs 71 cr of capex. Promoter group has bought every quarter and filed on 23-Nov-2026 that it reached 71.25%, two days before the Cabinet decision and near the 52-week low. Published at MEDIUM confidence with the negatives stated at equal length: the capex is already past its prospectus deadline of March 2026 with Rs 38.60 cr of Rs 70.07 cr unspent at 30-Sep-2026 (Monitoring Agency Report); crane dealers have been stuck at 25 for three quarters against the 50 needed; FY27 guidance of 20-25% is running at +12.4% at the half-year; ROE is 4.15%; the operating cycle is 240 days; and ACE - 63% of the mobile-crane market by its own 12-Nov-2026 deck - grew Q2 volumes 2,348 to 2,812 at a 19.31% margin while Indo Farm's crane revenue went sideways at 12.63%. Median daily turnover is Rs 11.0 lakh, below the playbook's own Rs 25 lakh floor, and that is in the red flags. **Whether pick-and-carry cranes are even eligible for the scheme is unknown** - the guidelines are unpublished and the news-reported product list names TBMs, excavators, ship-to-shore cranes and off-highway trucks, not pick-and-carry cranes. No part of the earnings table assumes the incentive.

note:
A heavy government day - the first in weeks where the PIB gate had real material - and one idea published from it.

**Lane one did the work.** 47 PIB releases, a Cabinet meeting, and seven decisions carrying a real outlay. The gate kept one (Kamarajar Port container terminal, Rs 4,288 cr) and the kept one was NOT the interesting one: its mapped small caps are defence-electronics and offshore-vessel companies with no filing showing they build container terminals, so exposure is unverified for every attached name and no card came from it. The interesting decisions were both UNMAPPED - a Rs 11,000 cr CIE manufacturing scheme and six new urea plants at Rs 54,000 cr. The first became today's idea and a new theme in theme_map.json; the second is carried to the next run because no supplier could be verified from its own filings today.

**The honest limit on the published card.** pib.gov.in is not on this sandbox's allow-list, so the release BODY was never read in this run. The title, ministry, PRID and the Rs 11,000 cr outlay come from the repository's own PIB reader on the Action runner at 18:57 IST; the scheme's mechanics come from news reports that disagree with each other; and the eligible-product list does not exist publicly yet, so whether pick-and-carry cranes even qualify is the card's first Unknown. No part of the card's earnings arithmetic assumes the incentive. What IS primary is the company: half its revenue is cranes (its own annual report), its crane plant is capacity-constrained at 80% utilisation (same document), and it is commissioning 3,600 cranes a year of new capacity for Rs 71.13 cr (its rating agency's press release). That is the idea; the scheme is why the name surfaced today.

**Lane two produced nothing, and the reason is a broken feed, not a quiet market.** 36 groups clear the up-threshold but the whole top of the table is computed off a WPI panel stuck at **April 2026** - seven months stale, because eaindustry.nic.in failed on the GitHub runner as well as here. A 1-month change ending in April is not a price that moved. Today's dated prints run the other way (Brent -20.2% on the month, copper -18.3%). The one group standing on fresher data is dye intermediates, off September customs numbers, with AksharChem and Shree Pushkar unpublished - first candidate for the next run. One mapping error found and logged for the owner, not edited: the paper group lists paper mills as beneficiaries of a rising waste-paper import price, which is their input cost.

**Lane three was thin.** 11 candidates, and the only hard trigger belonged to a name already published - whose 'order win' turned out, on reading the annexure, to be a Rs 12 cr related-party order put out under a press-release headline. The rest were volume breakouts with no filing to explain them, which the playbook watch-lists rather than researches.

**The sweep found more than the lanes did.** 92 cards swept, 17 filings opened, 16 updates written, three guidance lines rewritten. Two red flags worth the reader's attention: a promoter-group member at GK Energy reported for contra trades without pre-clearance, and Highway Infrastructure's related-party order. One structural change: Bhagyanagar's entire copper business has been demerged into Tieramet, whose MD told his first call that the record Rs 1,000 cr quarter will not repeat next quarter because copper has fallen - the card's own mechanism, running in reverse.
